title: Entropy Forge — a lossless compression lab
description: An interactive information-theory and data-compression laboratory, built from scratch with zero dependencies. It measures Shannon entropy (order-0/1/2) and the theoretical compression floor, then implements and visualises every major lossless codec family — a Huffman coder with a live code-tree and canonical length table; a genuine Witten–Neal–Cleary integer arithmetic coder (32-bit registers, E1/E2/E3 renormalisation, pending-bit underflow) with adaptive order-0 and order-1 models that hug the entropy bound; LZ77/LZSS sliding-window matching with a colour-coded parse map; LZW with a self-building dictionary and variable-width codes (KwKwK handled); and a full bzip2-style Burrows–Wheeler pipeline (suffix-sorted BWT with LF-mapping inverse, move-to-front, run-length, arithmetic). Composite codecs assemble the real formats — DEFLATE-lite (LZ77 tokens entropy-coded) and bzip-lite. And now THE ACTUAL FORMAT: a from-scratch, RFC 1951-compliant DEFLATE codec — the algorithm inside gzip, zlib, PNG and ZIP — with a 32 KB hash-chain + lazy-matching LZ77 stage, all three block types (stored, the canned fixed Huffman code, and a dynamic Huffman code built by the lab's own package-merge and capped at 15 bits, its length tables run-length-compressed by the 19-symbol code-length alphabet), an auto-selector that emits the cheapest block, and a puff-style inflater. It gets DEFLATE's tricky bit order exactly right (fields pack LSB-first, Huffman codes MSB-first), wraps the payload in byte-exact gzip (RFC 1952) and zlib (RFC 1950) containers with from-scratch CRC-32 and Adler-32, and — the real proof — INTEROPERATES: the .gz it emits decompresses with the browser's own gunzip, the browser's gzip inflates here, and its auto encoder matches or beats zlib level 9 on the structured corpora. A dedicated DEFLATE & gzip page shows a live native-interop badge, a stored-vs-fixed-vs-dynamic block showdown, the 32 KB LZ parse map, the full dynamic-block anatomy (HLIT/HDIST/HCLEN + the live literal/length, distance and code-length code tables), and an annotated gzip container hex dump. It also implements tANS / FSE — the multiply-free, table-driven Finite State Entropy coder inside Zstandard and Apple's LZFSE — sharing rANS's normalised model but coding by a finite-state machine of lookups and shifts alone, cross-verified to land within a few bytes of rANS on every input. At the far frontier it now implements CONTEXT MIXING — the PAQ/lpaq family that underpins the strongest general-purpose compressors ever measured: a bit-level predictor that runs a panel of models (order-0..6 byte contexts, a word model, and a longest-match model), each keeping an adaptive per-context probability, and blends their opinions in the log-odds domain with a context-selected LOGISTIC MIXER trained by online logistic regression, then refines the blend through two SSE (secondary-symbol-estimation) adaptive-probability-map stages before a carryless 32-bit BINARY arithmetic coder spends −log₂p bits per bit — with nothing transmitted but the stream, since the decoder rebuilds the identical panel and replays every update. Across the corpus it is the strongest all-rounder, winning most inputs outright and coming within a byte or two of PPM on the rest. Its own lab page shows a live bits-per-byte learning curve, the mixer's signed per-model trust weights, per-model accuracy, a bit-by-bit prediction ribbon, and the match length climbing over repetitive data. And it now implements LZMA — the algorithm inside 7-Zip and xz, and the moment the lab's two halves finally join: instead of Huffman-coding an LZ token stream, LZMA feeds EVERY decision (is-this-a-match, is-it-a-repeat, the length, the distance slot, the literal byte) into a single from-scratch adaptive BINARY RANGE CODER whose 11-bit probabilities are chosen by a rich context — a 12-STATE machine remembering whether recent packets were literals or matches, the low position bits, the previous byte, and, on the literal right after a match, the byte that would have been copied (matched-literal coding). The four most-recent match distances live in an MRU list (rep0..rep3) recoded with a handful of context bits instead of the full distance machinery — the reason LZMA crushes data that revisits offsets — while new distances code a 6-bit magnitude slot plus a reverse-tree of near bits or direct + 4-bit align bits, and match lengths (2..273) take a low/mid/high split; an HC4 match finder (hash2/hash3 heads + a hash4 chain) with a lazy, rep-preferring parse feeds it. The encoder AUTO-TUNES its literal/position model — it races six (lc, lp, pb) presets and ships the smallest, storing the choice in the one-byte LZMA properties (the exact byte .xz records, so the stream is self-describing), which shrinks every corpus for a single transmitted byte. Its lab page lays the coder bare — a size race against every other from-scratch codec, the packet stream coloured by literal/new-match/rep0..3 with width proportional to output bytes, the distance-source breakdown that makes the rep list's payoff visible, and the live 12-state transition table. On the benchmark it is the strongest DICTIONARY coder, winning the repetitive corpus outright and leading gzip/DEFLATE/bzip on the structured ones. A Benchmark page races all codecs — real gzip, tANS, context mixing and LZMA included — on eight corpora against the entropy floor, every result verified by a full decode; a live Self-test round-trips every codec across the corpus plus adversarial edge cases (empty, single-symbol, all-256-bytes, long runs, pseudo-random) — 617 in-browser checks plus 28 native-gzip cross-checks — and offline fuzzes of thousands of cases (validated directly against Node's zlib, a 400-case context-mixing fuzz, and a 3,000-case LZMA fuzz across five structure classes) found zero mismatches.
